title: Implementation of Smart Nation and Cashless Payment for Public Services
what_it_is: Implementation of Smart Nation and Cashless Payment for Public Services

sections.label: Elderly and cashless payments
sections.summary: Questions ask how the Government will help seniors adopt cashless payments, which public services will go cashless, how to lower e-payment costs, and how to monitor security risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked	the Prime Minister how does the Government plan to help the elderly get ready for a Smart nation and not be left out in our endeavour towards a cashless future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked	the Prime Minister (a) what are the upcoming areas of public services that the Government plans to implement cashless payments; (b) how will the Government help seniors who may have difficulties adopting e-payments in those areas; and (c) how can the overall costs and charges of e-payments be lowered for the merchants and end consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: asked	the Prime Minister (a) whether there will be an effort to identify any potential increase in security and personal safety risks that arise from an increase in electronic payment options, including scamming, loansharking and blackmail; and (b) what steps are being taken to monitor these risks, inform the public and mitigate these risks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For example, under e-payments, the Payments Council has set up an industry task force to establish a common Quick Response (QR) code standard for Singapore, or SGQR, by the end of 2017.

sections.label: PayNow mobile number transfers
sections.summary: PayNow lets Singaporeans pay one another across accounts in different banks using only the recipient's mobile number.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For example, PayNow enables Singaporeans to pay one another, across accounts held in different banks using just the recipient's mobile number.

sections.label: Workgroup digital readiness recommendations
sections.summary: The Workgroup will propose strategies to improve Singaporeans' digital readiness by early next year, reinforcing initiatives like the Silver Infocomm Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The Workgroup, in its recommendations, will propose strategies to improve digital readiness in Singaporeans, by early next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: These will reinforce existing initiatives, such as the Silver Infocomm Initiative (SII) by IMDA which has reached out to more than 130,000 seniors to promote information technology (IT) awareness and literacy.

sections.label: Singaporeans resilient to change
sections.summary: Singaporeans are resilient enough to weather this change and will come out the better for it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Singaporeans are resilient enough to weather this change and will come out the better for it.

sections.label: Balanced approach to e-payment proposals
sections.summary: The question asks the Government's approach to such a proposal and other companies' proposals, needing balance between regulation and opportunities for innovative solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State the approach the Government will take in considering such a proposal and whether the Government will be looking at other proposals submitted by other companies as well?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We need to have a balanced approach between complete regulation and creating opportunities for innovative solutions from a number of players, including banking and non-banking institutions.

sections.label: MAS studies unified e-payment proposals
sections.summary: MAS studies all proposals carefully, requiring a common platform, interoperable standards, competition, and compliance, without lowering risk management quality or allowing a fragmented ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On the Member's second question about the submission of a unified e-payment system from Razer, MAS receives quite a lot of proposals and we study all the proposals carefully.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: There is a common platform, a series of interoperable standards, space for competition and adherence to the regulations and compliance with the financial regulations that are already in place.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We cannot afford to lower that bar of quality in terms of risk and risk management, and we cannot afford an e-payment ecosystem that is fragmented and not interoperable.

sections.label: Targeted services and onboarding tracking
sections.summary: Services specifically target this group, with extra effort to engage and onboard people, and the percentage onboarded is tracked.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We do have services which are specifically targeted at this group of people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We are, in all our efforts, taking some extra effort to engage, to onboard people, and we are tracking the percentage of people who come onboard in our various services.

sections.label: Government digital service standards
sections.summary: The Government has digital service standards for consistent userability, accessibility and mobile-ready websites.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, the Government does have a set of digital service standards, so that services should have a consistent level of userability, accessibility, should be mobile-ready, websites especially.

sections.label: Web Content Accessibility guidelines compliance
sections.summary: All Government digital services must comply with the Web Content Accessibility guidelines, an international standard for accessible web content for persons with disability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: All Government digital services must also comply with the Web Content Accessibility guidelines which are an international standard for making web content accessible to persons with disability.

sections.label: Secure e-payments and trust
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked if it will devise a system, and e-payments must be secure and trusted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is the Ministry ready to look at some of these issues and devise some system?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We do have to ensure that e-payments are secure and have security behind them, and people trust in them.

sections.label: Unified ecosystem and fraud detection
sections.summary: A unified, unfragmented ecosystem is lacking and being moved towards, while MAS has systems to detect and deter fraud and threats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: What we do not have is a unified, unfragmented ecosystem and that is what we are moving towards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: MAS has a number of systems and processes in place to detect and deter fraud as well as threats.
